newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOTM to securitise loans to Japanese companies.
newsitem.headline: BOTM to securitise loans to Japanese companies.

text.p: Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd plans to securitise in the eurobond market 105 billion yen worth of loans it made to Japanese companies, a bank official said on Monday.
A special purpose company to be set up in the Cayman Islands by BOTM will issue 95 billion yen worth of euroyen and eurodollar bonds and 10 billion yen worth of subordinated euroyen bonds.
Thirty-four loan contracts with 27 Japanese firms from a wide range of industries will be used as collateral for those bonds, the official said.
The bonds, maturing in three years, will be sold to European, U.S. and Asian institutional investors, including buyers in Japan.

This securitisation plan, which will be the biggest done by any Japanese bank in the eurobond market, will allow Tokyo-Mitsubishi to fully remove 105 billion yen worth of loan assets from its balance sheet, the official said.
Bank analysts say Japanese banks are aiming to cut loan assets as a way to meet capital adequacy rules set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
